newsitem.title: UK: CalEnergy swoops on Northern Electric. [corrected 09:53 gmt]
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy swoops on Northern Electric. [corrected 09:53 gmt]

text.p: CE Electric UK, 70-percent owned by CalEnergy of the United States, has made an offer of 630 pence a share cash for the UK's Northern Electric.

The offer values Northern Electric's ordinary share capital at 651 million stg. CalEnergy is offering 103 pence for each preference share, valuing Northern Electric's preference share capital at 115 million stg.
"Our strategy is to become a leading global provider of a full range of energy services," said CalEnergy's chairman and chief executive David Sokol in a statement on Monday.
"Northern Electric meets all our criteria for the further development of our business. I believe that our offer represents a unique opportunity for shareholders, employees and customers."

Regional utility Northern Electric successfully fended off a hostile bid from Trafalgar House (now owned by Kvaerner), using an agressive bid defence making use of a series of special dividend payouts. In June, Northern reported pre-exceptional pre-tax profits of 117.2 million stg, down from 140.7 million stg the year before.

CalEnergy, which has made the bid together with U.S.-based construction, mining and telecommunications group Peter Kiewit Sons, has assets of more than $3.5 billion. Sokol was appointed head of the company in 1991, since when CalEnergy's market capitalisation has grown from $200 million to $1.9 billion.
(Corrects above paragraph to clarify that CalEnergy is making the bid together with Peter Kiewit Sons. It is CalEnergy which has assets of over $3.5 billion, not both companies combined.)
